checks.what: US loss to spanish-empire in February 1821 of Colorado and the Wyoming strip south of 42N lying west of 106.33W (540 cells, 136,566 km2; about 330 of them were US-held). The page gives the line along the Arkansas 'to its source', then due north or south to 42N, then along 42N. It places the source at 39 deg 15' 30" N, 106 deg 20' 38" W, and says the treaty was 'officially made effective on February 22, 1821'. The 106.33 edge is within 1 km of 106.344. In Colorado the Arkansas lies east of that meridian below its source, so all the land cut is on the Spanish side. In the trial, first-mexican-empire takes it from Spain by R2 (330 cell-years, 1821).

russian-empire occupation_end 1828 against ottoman-empire over Moldova (130 cells). The page: the Treaty of Bucharest, signed by the Sultan in May 1812, by which 'the Ottoman Empire acknowledged the Russian annexation' of the land 'between the Prut and Dniester'. The published draft had owner russian-empire, occupier ottoman-empire, 132 cells, since 1828. The trial shows the relation gone at the end of 1829, Khotyn included, and the Russian occupations of Moldavia (144) and Wallachia (265) untouched. The render of 1829 shows Bessarabia plain Russian.

circassia occupation_end 1822 against russian-empire over Kabardin-Balkar (49 cells). The page: Kabarda 'formally recognized Russian suzerainty' after 1779; in 1820 it was 'declared property of the Russian government'; it was 'placed under Russian military rule in 1822, as Kabardia eventually fully fell'. The published draft had owner russian-empire, occupier circassia, 47 cells, 1822-1864 (roles reversed). The trial shows it gone, and the render of 1829 shows Kabarda plain Russian. The same region is used in the dossier's ledger/2 and ledger/5.

republic-of-peru contest_start 1826 against gran-colombia over Loreto (1302 cells). The page: Gran Colombia's claims to Jaen and Maynas date 'from colonial times'; the Armistice of Piura (10 July 1829) recognized 'Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas as Peruvian territories'. In the trial the Peru/Gran Colombia contest grows from 146 to 1411 cells in 1826-1828 and closes with ledger/7 in July 1829 (no open contest at the end of 1829). The diagnosis in the note is slightly off: in 1822-1825 the contest held only 146 cells, so Loreto was never contested before (Peru held no Loreto cells in 1822), not lost in 1825. The fix is still what dossier ledger/1 intends. The page does not say who held Maynas on the ground (confidence 2 is right).
